newsitem.title: THAILAND: Mine kills five pro-Rangoon Karens at Thai border.
newsitem.headline: Mine kills five pro-Rangoon Karens at Thai border.

text.p: At least five members of the pro-Rangoon Democratic Karen Buddhist Army (DKBA) were killed on Tuesday by a landmine as they were about to attack Karen refugees camps in Thailand, Thai police said.

They told Reuters that the five were part of a 50-member DKBA guerrilla group that crossed the Moei River that marks the border and were heading to the Kwaymong refugee camp when they set off the mine.
The mine wounded several others. Fellow guerrillas dragged the bodies across the river back into Burma, they said.
The mines were planted on the bank of the Moei River to thwart DKBA attacks on the camps about 22 km (12 miles) from Mae Sot, police sources said.
Kwaymong camp houses about 4,000 Karen refugees who are mainly family members of the DKBA's rival group, the predominantly-Christian Karen National Union (KNU).
The DKBA split from the KNU and defected to Burmese troops in early 1995 and has been harassing the KNU since.
Some 70,000 Karen refugees, KNU family members and followers have lived in camps in Thailand for more than 10 years.
